title: What are you guys using to create bots?
author: sparkyr47
selftext: Hi guys I’m new here currently working as an electrician. I’m fairly versed in daytrading the manual way as well as using multiple ais (chat gpt, broke, ect). But I really have no idea how to rope them together to actually create a working trading hit that gets results does anyone have some beginner advice. Anything would be appreciated thanks guys!

comments.author: Jump_in_Jack

Currently decentralized is only solana tokens.. but centralized runs Bitunix and Kraken api. It calculates fees into every trade and even does csv files tracking for tax season.

comments.author: Individual-Quote-958
comments.body: Honestly I'd start without AI making decisions. Pick one simple rule you already trade by hand, backtest it with real fees and slippage, then paper trade it through your broker's API for a few weeks. ChatGPT is fine for helping you write the code, but I wouldn't let it pick trades until the basic rule works. I'd also never give a third party bot your private keys or withdrawal permissions.

comments.author: k1_r1
comments.body: +1 to starting without the ai making decisions. the part everyone skips is writing the rule down precisely enough that a computer can test it. "buy when it looks oversold" isnt a rule, "buy when the 14 day rsi closes under 30 and price is above the 200 day" is. once you have that, chatgpt or claude can write the backtest in python, just read what it gives you because they love quietly peeking at future data. i work on portfoliolab which does the plain english to backtest part and has paper accounts so you can watch it run before any real money goes in. but the rule is the hard part, not the tool

comments.author: Mysterious-Man88
comments.body: I use Claude. It’s worked pretty well

comments.author: br-hm
comments.body:
I use Claude Code, it’s pretty seamless nowadays with putting strategies into code, but it really does take a good amount of understanding strategies yourself in order to find profitable ones.

I download tick data from QDM, put it into MT5, tell Claude my strategy idea and have it write code into MQL5 (MT5’s coding language), and start backtesting and optimizing from there
